analysis:
Examined the Autopilot wire-protocol additions, the decoder, the busy-reason enums, ProviderState changes, and the ProviderLoop+Capacity hunks. No concrete security regression found in the supplied evidence.

ModelAutopilot.swift adds optional snapshot fields (capabilities, adopted_models, held_models, busy_reasons/busy_reason/busy_since_ms, transition_stalls, download_storage), a hold_seconds field on ModelAutopilotCommand, and a status detail field. All new snapshot fields are optional and decoded with decodeIfPresent, so older peers stay compatible. Download storage (disk free, reserve, usage) and hold data are provider-reported to the trusted coordinator. They expose no prompt data, keys, or attestation material. They are minor disk-metrics disclosure, which is already in the coordinator-trusted channel (TB-002). Busy reasons are a closed enum, but the snapshot fields are plain Strings, so unknown values are not validated at decode time. This is benign for outbound reporting.

hold_seconds is a coordinator-supplied value documented as 0...86_400. The range enforcement is not visible in these units. The consuming code (autopilotHeldWeightBytes, sweepAutopilotCachedBuilds, refreshAutopilotDownloadStorage, superviseTransitions, refreshAutopilotInventoryRegistration) is outside the supplied hunks, so I could not verify clamping, hold-expiry handling, or whether adopted models and holds could be used to keep memory pinned and starve serving (availability, T-029-like). The coordinator is trusted and hop-by-hop, so the risk is bounded. Integration should confirm the clamp and that the hold does not bypass the load gate or the weight-hash and attestation checks.

CoordinatorClientState.swift replaces the autopilotInventory setter with an atomic publishModelAutopilot(snapshot, inventory) plus modelAutopilotRegistration. That improves consistency between selected_models and the registered inventory, and the lock discipline is preserved. The new registeredAutopilotInventoryIDs is only a mirror. ProviderLoop+Capacity.swift now subtracts held weight bytes from reclaimable MLX memory, a conservative change for capacity advertisement.

New downloads capability (inventory_downloads): prefetch_model downloads builds outside ordinary serving into an Autopilot set. The download and verification logic is not in the supplied units. It touches A-004 and T-012/T-027 (weight integrity, weight-hash verification). Needs review of whether downloaded builds are hash-verified before being adopted or advertised.
